title: Rochdale Asda worker's kindness a 'breath of fresh air' for widowed customer
excerpt: Saheda times her help around an older customer's shopping trips after the woman lost her husband, scanning and packing her shopping and stopping for a chat.
body:
A worker at Asda's Rochdale store has been praised for looking out for an older customer after the woman was widowed.

Saheda first noticed something had changed when the customer, who used to shop with her husband, stopped coming in for a while. When she next saw her, the woman was shopping with her daughter, and the pair told her what had happened.

The daughter lives in London and was worried about how her mother would cope on her own. Saheda promised to look after her and told her which days she works, so the customer could time her visits for when Saheda would be there.

Now, when the customer comes in, Saheda scans and packs her shopping, fetches her a chair and makes time for a chat.

The customer told the store's customer manager, Dave, how much the help meant to her. Dave said: "The lady told me that ever since she lost her husband three months ago, Saheda has been like a breath of fresh air in her life every time she shops – not just because of the help she offers, but as an emotional support and somebody to chat to."

Saheda said: "I used to see the lady come in with her husband all the time and then didn't see her for a while. Then I saw her shopping with her daughter, and they told me what had happened. I told her to come and see me every time she came in... and she does. We have a good chat and I help her, as she does struggle a bit."

She added: "She thanks me every single time and I go, 'no, you don't need to thank me'. It's sweet, though. I like to think that somebody would do that for my own mum. I always think too that one day I could be in that position. It doesn't cost anything to be pleasant and kind, does it?"

For someone adjusting to life alone after a bereavement, a familiar face on a weekly errand can make a real difference, and the help Saheda gives costs nothing but a little time.

Source: account supplied to Rochdale Daily. Photograph: supplied.
